interim_updates.note_text: Central Finance Company PLC (CFIN), a licensed finance company (NBFI, FYE 31 March), reported Group profit before tax of Rs.3,801.6mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 8% YoY from Rs.3,511.1mn, and Group PAT of Rs.2,894.9mn, up 12% YoY from Rs.2,578.2mn. Total operating income rose 23% to Rs.5,473.5mn (2025: Rs.4,463.4mn), driven by net interest income growth of 10% (Rs.3,713.7mn vs Rs.3,368.6mn, as interest income grew 24% to Rs.5,498.5mn but interest expense grew faster at 69% to Rs.1,784.7mn on higher funding costs/volumes), a 468% jump in other income/losses to Rs.419.9mn (2025: Rs.73.9mn), and operating lease income up 32% to Rs.525.8mn. Impairment reversal (a credit to the P&L) nearly halved to Rs.253.1mn (2025: Rs.495.5mn, -49%), which is a real headwind to the growth rate even though the current period still books a net reversal rather than a charge. Operating expenses rose 25% to Rs.2,345.4mn on personnel costs (+14%) and premises/establishment/other expenses (+38%, which also carries the Group's forex and non-parent interest costs per Note 9). By segment, the core Leasing/hire purchase/loans book (the dominant segment) grew its segment result 8% to Rs.2,618.4mn (2025: Rs.2,428.3mn); Manufacturing segment result rose 35% to Rs.265.3mn (2025: Rs.196.8mn); Insurance broking rose 54% to Rs.199.0mn (2025: Rs.129.6mn); but the Investments segment result fell 40% to Rs.428.0mn (2025: Rs.712.8mn), driven by that segment's interest income falling 42% (Rs.313.0mn vs Rs.537.2mn) and other income/losses falling 22% (Rs.153.1mn vs Rs.195.2mn). Share of profit of equity-accounted investees (held at Group level, not separately named in this filing) fell 4% to Rs.974.4mn (2025: Rs.1,011.0mn), and while it did not move the P&L much, the same investee drove a large negative OCI swing: the fair value reserve attributable to the investee's own OCI moved from +Rs.213.9mn a year ago to -Rs.882.1mn this quarter, pulling Group total comprehensive income down 28% to Rs.2,012.9mn (2025: Rs.2,792.2mn) even as reported PAT rose 12%. Company (standalone) PBT and PAT both fell YoY (-5% and -4% respectively) despite Company revenue growth of 22%, because Company operating expenses rose 30% and the Company's impairment reversal nearly halved (Rs.252.7mn vs Rs.496.5mn) -- the Group's better headline growth is being driven by the non-lending subsidiaries and the associate/OCI items, not by the core Company-level lending business.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for CFIN -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. short_term_borrowings/long_term_borrowings left blank in the financial_statements rows because the filing discloses only a single combined 'Interest bearing borrowings' line with no current/non-current maturity split on the face of this interim statement -- omitted rather than guessed. Company-standalone EPS is not printed by the filing and was derived arithmetically (documented in that row's notes).
interim_updates.takeaway: Group PAT growth of 12% overstates the strength of the core lending business: standalone Company PAT actually fell 4% YoY, and the quarter's operating income growth leaned heavily on a swing in 'other income' (+468%) and non-lending subsidiaries (Manufacturing +35%, Insurance broking +54%), while the year-on-year impairment reversal roughly halved from Rs.495.5mn to Rs.253.1mn -- a shrinking tailwind that will need replacing by underlying income growth in coming quarters. Separately, a large negative fair-value swing at the equity-accounted investee level (fair value reserve -Rs.882.1mn vs +Rs.213.9mn a year ago) meant total comprehensive income fell 28% even as the P&L profit line rose.

operational_highlights: Group Total operating income Rs.5,473.5mn, +23% YoY (2025: Rs.4,463.4mn); Group PBT Rs.3,801.6mn, +8% YoY; Group PAT Rs.2,894.9mn, +12% YoY.
Net interest income +10% YoY to Rs.3,713.7mn as interest expense (+69% to Rs.1,784.7mn) grew much faster than interest income (+24% to Rs.5,498.5mn).
Impairment reversal nearly halved YoY to Rs.253.1mn (2025: Rs.495.5mn, -49%) -- a shrinking earnings tailwind.
Gross Stage 3 loans ratio improved to 1.53% (30.06.2025: 2.09%) but Stage 3 impairment coverage fell to 61.29% (2025: 77.29%) and total impairment coverage fell to 1.82% (2025: 3.78%).
Tier 1 and Total Capital Adequacy Ratios remain very high at 33.18% and 31.78% respectively (minimums 10%/14%), though both fell YoY from 43.04%/40.90% as the balance sheet grew faster than capital.

Interest-bearing borrowings rose sharply to Rs.30,098,870k from Rs.20,685,082k at 31 March 2026 (+46% in the quarter alone), funding loan/lease book growth; deposits grew more modestly (+1.2% quarter-on-quarter to Rs.49,407,526k).
key_drivers: Investments segment result -40% YoY (Rs.428.0mn vs Rs.712.8mn) on a 42% fall in that segment's interest income (Rs.313.0mn vs Rs.537.2mn) and a 22% fall in other income/losses (Rs.153.1mn vs Rs.195.2mn).

Manufacturing segment result +35% YoY (Rs.265.3mn vs Rs.196.8mn) and Insurance broking +54% YoY (Rs.199.0mn vs Rs.129.6mn) -- the diversified non-lending subsidiaries, not the core lending book, drove most of the Group's YoY growth.

Fair value reserve swung from +Rs.213.9mn (Q1 FY2025/26) to -Rs.882.1mn (this quarter), entirely via 'share of equity accounted investee, net of tax' in other comprehensive income -- this is why total comprehensive income (-28% YoY) diverged sharply from reported PAT (+12% YoY).
Impairment reversal fell from Rs.495.5mn to Rs.253.1mn (-49% YoY), a meaningful drag on the pace of operating income growth even though it remained a net credit rather than a charge.
